## TL;DR

I completed the Inputs and Context page QA pass at desktop and phone widths using
headless Playwright against the auth-less task worktree server. The pages fit at
1280px and 375px, the screenshot picker and preview worked without submitting a
test record, and the Docs, Skills, Discover, and History tabs loaded without
horizontal overflow. The pass exposed a genuine state-reporting bug: failed list
requests could look like successful empty results. Inputs and Context now show
retryable errors and distinguish loading, failure, and a real empty result.

## Work and rationale

I started from the task’s acceptance criteria and ran `just serve-noauth 7272`
inside this task worktree. The server build completed and the preview build
identified itself as a preview. I used Playwright Chromium in headless mode; no
visible browser or main checkout was used. The initial browse covered Inputs
list and board modes and the Context Docs, Skills, Discover, and History tabs at
1280 × 900 and 375 × 900. I also opened an input detail drawer, used the file
picker to select a small PNG, confirmed its preview appeared, and removed the
draft attachment. I did not submit an input, create a document, or install a
skill, so this QA pass left no test content in the project.

Responsive checks found the document width equal to the viewport at both
target sizes. The Inputs list, board, detail drawer, and screenshot picker all
fit on a 375px viewport. Context remained within the viewport on all four tabs.
Existing documents appeared in the Docs tree and selected content rendered in
the preview. No uncaught page errors or console errors occurred in this normal
flow.

The important finding came from simulating API failures rather than treating an
empty project as proof of error handling. `refreshInputs()` caught network
errors and returned no result, leaving the store’s empty initial list in place.
Inputs therefore showed its successful empty-state message after a failed
request. The docs store also returned `false` on `/api/docs` failure, but the
Context view did not use that result and presented “No docs found.” while the
request was loading or had failed. In each case, the screen implied the project
contained no data when the service had not answered successfully.

I made the Inputs store return a boolean from `refreshInputs()`, preserving
existing data on failure and informing the view whether the latest refresh
succeeded. Inputs now keeps a local load-error flag, shows a concise error and
Retry action in both list and board modes, and clears the error after a
successful retry. Context’s docs store now exposes loading and error state. The
Docs tab renders a loading message while data is pending, a retry action after
failure, and “No docs found” only after a successful empty response. The
existing Context refresh method continues to refresh the document tree and now
drives the shared error state through the same store method.

## Approaches tried

I first exercised the real pages with their ordinary worktree data and checked
the viewport bounds. I used Playwright file selection to cover the native
screenshot picker and preview UI, then cleared the draft rather than submitting
it. For failure states, I routed requests through Playwright and deliberately
returned 503 responses. The first attempt let a second background Inputs fetch
succeed before I inspected the result, so the error disappeared quickly. I
changed the probe to hold all matching requests at 503 until the Retry action
was pressed. That made the failure and recovery states deterministic and
confirmed that both pages recover after the API is allowed through.

I added focused regression cases for the Inputs view and docs store. The Inputs
view test verifies the failure copy replaces the empty-state message and that a
retry clears the alert and returns to the legitimate empty state. The docs store
test verifies the failed load exposes an error and ends loading, then clears
the error after a successful retry. The configured test script, rather than a
bare Vitest invocation, was needed because the direct invocation did not load
the Vue SFC test plugin.

## Challenges and blockers

There was no product or repository blocker. The initial browser failure probe
waited for an alert while a second request had already recovered, and so it
timed out. I inspected request traffic and corrected the route to keep the
failure active until a deliberate retry. A first direct Vitest command also
bypassed the repository’s Vue test setup and failed before running the Inputs
test; the repository’s `bun run test` wrapper then ran the affected tests
successfully. These were harness adjustments, not unresolved failures.

The simulated 503 responses produced expected browser resource-error messages.
Those were intentional network failures, not application exceptions; the
normal flow and post-retry flows had no uncaught page errors. The QA screenshots
are stored under the task worktree’s ignored `.repoos/qa-1204/` directory for
local reference.

## Key learnings

An empty-state check must distinguish three outcomes: a request still in
progress, a request that failed, and a successful response containing no data.
Silently retaining an initial empty array makes those cases indistinguishable
unless the store exposes request state to the view. A retry should clear its
error only after the refreshed data arrives; a failure should preserve useful
data already loaded. The Inputs store change follows this rule without clearing
the existing list. The docs store surfaces a shared status so both initial load
and manual refresh render consistent guidance.

The route interception also showed why an API failure probe must control all
matching requests: startup and retry/background refreshes can issue more than
one request, hiding a transient error before an assertion observes it. Holding
the response until the user action made the exercise repeatable. Final focused
test execution passed 13 tests. The required
`REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` also passed: formatting, lint, build,
UI guards, rendered contrast, browser smoke, and the remote changed-path test
suite (1,705 tests). RepoOS recorded its WIP checkpoint automatically for
remote validation; I did not stage or commit files manually.
